title: How to Get a Docusign API Key and Handle Limits
summary: Docusign API integrations use REST endpoints to manage agreements.
body_markdown:
## Docusign API pricing and rate limits by plan


$600 a year for Starter, $3,600 for Intermediate, $5,760 for Advanced: those are the costs, set by the plan's envelope allowance, which means you pay more for a bigger allowance.


The rate limits that push back at 2am are a separate matter, and one the figures below don't settle.


### Docusign API per-envelope pricing and plan allowances


At $600 a year, Starter allows 40 envelopes a month, according to[Nodshake](https://www.nodshake.com/guides/docusign-api-alternatives) . That works out to about $1.25 per envelope.


**The allowance is the number to watch** : a retry loop that resends on every error can use up the month before anyone is awake to see it.


The chart shows annual cost for the two plans with a stated monthly allowance, meaning you can calculate the cost-per-transaction for each tier.


For $3,600 a year, Intermediate allows 100 envelopes a month, per[Nodshake](https://www.nodshake.com/guides/docusign-api-alternatives) . That's $3 per envelope, so 2.5 times the allowance costs six times the price.


Advanced costs more and buys no more envelopes: it is also listed at 100 envelopes a month, at $5,760 a year. Nothing in that figure buys more envelopes, so the extra $2,160 over Intermediate pays for features, not volume.


Whoever owns the budget should know which feature justified it.


### Documented rate limits and burst limits


I have no confirmed per-plan rate or burst figure to quote, so none appears here. Docusign's developer documentation is where to check current limits, and you should treat anything you read elsewhere as unverified.


When one team runs a batch job, another team's signing flow can slow down, because limits apply per account and every integration sharing it draws on the same budget.


When you exceed a limit, expect the API to refuse calls with an error until the window passes. Back off and retry later instead of retrying immediately.


### Docusign API polling versus Connect webhooks


Every status poll on a timer counts against the account's call budget, because polling asks Docusign for an envelope's status each time. With many open envelopes, polling spends that budget on "no change" answers.


Connect is Docusign's webhook feature: it pushes a notification when status changes, so you spend calls only on events.


The cost is an endpoint that must stay reachable and someone who owns it. If that endpoint is down, you miss notifications unless you reconcile with an occasional status check.


Activepieces flows start from triggers, and the catalogue is large enough that its integration list is the place to look for Docusign triggers and actions before you settle for a timer loop.


Describe the process in the built-in chat, such as "when an envelope is completed, update our record", and the flow it publishes shows up in your account as an ordinary flow you can open step by step, with a run trace for each execution showing where a call succeeded or failed, under the same RBAC and audit logs as a flow someone built by hand.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production, and the core is MIT-licensed, so the code behind each integration sits in the open source monorepo alongside 750 integrations.
